To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the relativistic optical model is a useful approximation for the scattering of medium—energy nucleons from nuclei; (ii) the nonrelativistic approximation is not valid for the scattering of high-energy nucleons; (iii) the relativistic approximation is not applicable to the scattering of low—energy nucleons; (iv) relativistic kinematics is important for the scattering of nucleons from nuclei, but relativistic kinematics alone does not provide the complete description of relativistic effects;

(i) the Dirac equation is not relevant to the description of medium-energy nucleonic collisions, (ii) the Dirac optical model is ambiguous, and (iii) the Dirac impulse approximation is not valid for medium-energy nucleonic reactions.

(1) The Dirac equation is not a good approximation to the Schrödinger equation for nucleon—nuclear scattering, and (2) The Dirac optical model is a poor approximation to the Schrodinger optical model.
